analysis:
Both changed files are test-only: InstalledSessionCheck.swift (head lines 984-986) and DistributedInstalledLanesTests.swift (new test at head lines 36-61). No production source is in this batch, so no auth, attestation, encryption or data-exposure control is changed here.

What the tests assert: the Gemma 4 pipeline with serial prefill defaults to 4 batch lanes, and the environment gains a batch-lanes switch set to gemma4PipelineBatchLanes. A saved one-chunk-lookahead schedule keeps one lane. Private images, non-pipeline modes and all other lane adapters keep their prior defaults. A cancelled Gemma lane retires alone.

Threat-model relevance: the production change implied by these tests (DistributedInstalledPlan.defaultBatchLanes and batchLanesSwitch) raises concurrency for Gemma pipeline serving. That touches TB-007 and residual-data topics such as T-028, and the prefix-cache cross-tenant behavior in T-041. Several requests would share a worker's lanes, so lane isolation, per-lane KV and cache-salt separation, and cancel/retire-alone semantics matter. The tests assert only retire-alone behavior and lane counts. They do not show per-request cacheSalt separation or KV clearing across lanes.

Remaining integration questions for the production diff, which is outside this batch: (1) whether the 4-lane Gemma path keeps per-request cache scope when it donates to or adopts from the SSD prefix cache; (2) whether per-lane memory is accounted in the KV grant so lanes cannot exhaust GPU memory (an availability concern); (3) whether private-image requests are rejected from the lane path. The tests assert that images yield nil lanes. No concrete regression is visible in the supplied test code. I set needs_deeper_review=false because the supplied evidence shows no uncertainty that affects a security conclusion, only unseen production code.
